ovulation-calculator.assumptionNote: Assumes ovulation 14 days before the next period - the standard calendar method. Real cycles vary.
benefits: Pinpoints the few days that actually matter each month.
Explains the biology simply - no app account needed.
Helps time conception attempts or understand your body.
Works for any cycle length, not just the textbook 28 days.

faqs.a: Very unlikely but not impossible. Sperm can survive up to 5 days, so intercourse just before the window can still lead to pregnancy. After ovulation plus one day, the egg is gone.
faqs.q: Can I get pregnant outside the fertile window?

faqs.a: The luteal phase (ovulation to next period) is the stable ~14 days. The follicular phase before ovulation is the variable part - that is why counting back from the next period works and counting forward from the last one does not.
Only roughly. Track 3-6 months of start dates, use the average, and treat the window as wider. Ovulation predictor kits or basal body temperature confirm the real day.
faqs.q: My cycle is irregular. Is this useful?

faqs.a: For regular cycles, within 1-2 days for most women. But 'most' is not 'all' - one shifted month is normal, especially with stress or illness.
faqs.q: How accurate is the fertile window?

faqs.a: Less well - PCOS often means irregular or absent ovulation. The calendar assumes ovulation happens, which PCOS disrupts. Talk to a doctor for proper tracking.
The 2-3 days before ovulation give the best odds - sperm are already waiting when the egg arrives. Daily intercourse across the window is fine too.

ovulation-calculator.formula:
Ovulation day = last period start + (cycle length - 14)
Fertile window = ovulation - 5 days ... ovulation + 1 day
Next period = last period start + cycle length

Example: last period 1 Jan, 28-day cycle
Ovulation = 1 Jan + (28 - 14) = 15 Jan
Fertile = 10 Jan to 16 Jan
Next period = 29 Jan
howTo: Enter the first day of your last period.
Enter your average cycle length (first day to first day, usually 21-35).
Your ovulation day, fertile window, and next period appear instantly.
For conception, aim for the 2-3 days before ovulation.
Track a few cycles and use your real average for better accuracy.
keyFacts: Ovulation = the ovary releasing an egg, about 14 days before the next period - not 14 days after the last one.
The fertile window = 5 days before ovulation through 1 day after. Sperm live up to 5 days; the egg lives 12-24 hours.
Cycle length varies (21-35 days is normal). The luteal phase after ovulation is the stable part, ~14 days.
Stress, illness, and travel can delay ovulation - the calendar is an estimate.
This method does not prevent pregnancy reliably on its own.
Irregular cycles need 3+ months of tracking before the pattern is useful.

ovulation-calculator.quickAnswer: Ovulation usually happens about 14 days before your next period. With a 28-day cycle starting 1 January, ovulation falls around 15 January and the fertile window runs 10-16 January (sperm survive up to 5 days, the egg about 1). Your next period is due around 29 January.
ovulation-calculator.tagline: Find your fertile window and ovulation day from your last period and cycle length.
ovulation-calculator.workedExample:
Last period started 1 January, average cycle 28 days:
1. Ovulation offset: 28 - 14 = 14 days after the start.
2. 1 Jan + 14 days = 15 January (ovulation day).
3. Fertile window: 15 Jan - 5 days = 10 Jan through 15 Jan + 1 = 16 Jan.
4. Next period: 1 Jan + 28 days = 29 January.

With a 32-day cycle instead: ovulation = 1 Jan + 18 = 19 Jan; fertile = 14-20 Jan.
